items.example_en: Excuse me, where is the station?
items.note: Slightly more formal than plain где; both are fine.

items.english: how do I get to (on foot)
items.example_en: How do I get to the museum?
items.note: пройти is on foot; проехать is by transport. к takes the dative.

items.example_en: Is it far from here on foot?
items.note: близко means near.

items.example_en: Go straight ahead to the traffic light.
Turn left after the church.
items.note: направо is to the right. слева and справа mean on the left and on the right.

items.example_en: The pharmacy is on the corner.
items.note: угол has a special locative form: на углу, not на угле.

items.example_en: Let's meet in front of the station.
items.note: A large terminus; a small stop is станция.

items.example_en: The bus stop is across the road.
items.note: From остановиться, to stop.

items.example_en: The shop is open until ten.
items.note: False friend: not a magazine, which is журнал.

items.example_en: There's a 24-hour pharmacy nearby.
Turn at the next crossroads.
I really like this neighbourhood.
items.note: нравиться works backwards: the thing liked is the subject.

items.example: Один билет туда и обратно до Твери.
items.example_en: One return ticket to Tver.
items.note: One way is билет в одну сторону.

items.example: Купить можно в кассе или онлайн.
items.example_en: You can buy at the ticket office or online.
items.note: Also the checkout in a shop.

items.example_en: The train departs from platform three.
items.note: с plus genitive for departing from.

items.example_en: I have a connection in Moscow.
items.note: Also used for changing metro lines.

items.example: Мы едем на метро, четвёртая линия.
items.example_en: We're taking the metro, line four.
items.note: на plus prepositional for the means of transport.

items.example_en: Check the timetable in the app.
The train is twenty minutes late.
items.note: на plus accusative for the size of the delay.

items.example_en: The flight is delayed by two hours.
Our flight has been cancelled.
items.note: Short passive participle, agreeing with the subject: отменён, отменена.

items.example_en: I missed the last train.
items.note: Literally to be late for the train. на plus accusative.

items.example_en: Sorry, I got lost on the way.
items.note: Past tense agrees with the speaker: заблудился, заблудилась.

items.example_en: When is the next bus?

items.example: Добрый вечер, у меня забронирован номер на фамилию Дюпон.
items.example_en: Good evening, I have a room booked under the name Dupont.
items.note: номер is a hotel room; комната is a room in a home.

items.example: Двухместный номер с видом на море.
items.example_en: A double room with a sea view.
items.note: одноместный is a single.

items.example_en: Is breakfast included in the price?
items.note: включён is a short passive participle.

items.example_en: Here's the room key.
items.note: от plus genitive expresses the key belonging to something.

items.example_en: What time is check-out tomorrow?
items.note: заезд is check-in, выезд is check-out.

items.english: I'd like to cancel the booking
items.example: Я хотел бы отменить бронь на пятницу.
items.example_en: I'd like to cancel the booking for Friday.
items.note: бы keeps it conditional and therefore polite.

items.example_en: I have a problem with the heating.
items.note: с plus instrumental: с отоплением.

items.example_en: The air conditioning doesn't work.
items.note: The same verb as to work at a job.

items.example: Не могли бы вы поменять номер?
items.example_en: Could you possibly change our room?
items.note: The negative conditional is the most polite Russian request form.

items.example_en: Can we leave our luggage at reception?
items.note: Collective singular, like English.

items.example: К счастью, у меня была страховка.
items.example_en: Luckily, I had insurance.
Thank you for your understanding.
items.note: за plus accusative for what you are thanking someone for.
